content.text:
You didn't write this code here. It's work that was already merged on GitHub, and your own `syncd watch` copied the files onto this Mac from another machine.

**What happened**

1. On Nov 18 a cloud Claude session made 10 fix commits on branch `claude/confident-cerf-nwwzz1`. You merged it as [PR #9](https://github.com/william-coronado/syncd/pull/9) at **23:15:34**.
2. Another machine that shares `~/dev` through the NAS pulled `main`.
3. At **23:20:23**, five minutes later, every one of these 23 files was created here in the same second. That's a bulk copy by a tool, not hand edits.
4. Your `~/dev/.syncdignore` excludes `.git/`. So syncd copied the updated files but not the commits. The local branch is still at `e766ebf`, 11 commits behind `origin/main`, so git shows the newer files as uncommitted changes.

**How I confirmed it**
- Each modified tracked file has exactly the same content as `origin/main`.
- Each of the 9 untracked files has the same git hash as its copy in `origin/main`.
- The only leftover differences are file permissions: 6 files changed from 644 to 755. That fits files copied through the SMB share. It isn't anything you edited.
- I found no stash, no other worktree and no local commits, so you have no local work of your own at risk.

I couldn't find a syncd log entry for the copy, because there are no log files in `~/.local/state/syncd/` beyond an empty `service.out.log`. The timing and identical contents are strong evidence on their own.

**Fixing it:** a plain `git pull` would refuse, because the untracked files are in the way. The files already match `origin/main`, so this is safe and loses nothing:

```bash
git reset --hard origin/main
```

That moves `main` to the merged PR and puts the permissions back to 644.

The same thing will happen whenever you pull on one machine and syncd copies the files to another. To avoid it, pull on each machine. You could also stop syncing git repositories through `~/dev`, or sync `.git/` as well, though that is risky with two machines writing to it.
